title: Create workspace platform philosophy script and HTML deck
measurement_note: Timing record was created after web-first intake, memory bootstrap, source reading, script writing, and HTML generation had already started. Early phases are intentionally not measured to avoid false precision. Verification phase includes measured command outputs where available.

phases.label: Web-first intake
phases.bottleneck_notes: Completed before timing record creation. Search focused on agent patterns, tracing, guardrails, AI risk management, and human-centered AI.

phases.label: Memory bootstrap
phases.bottleneck_notes: Completed before timing record creation; hot anchors guided philosophy, platform identity, and presentation-agent boundaries.

phases.label: Requirements, specs, and source notes
phases.bottleneck_notes: Added the presentation spec, plan, tasks, validation, traceability, requirements entry, source notes, provenance, and plan evidence.

phases.label: Script and deck generation
phases.bottleneck_notes: Largest unmeasured phase. Created the full Korean script first, then compressed it into a 24-slide deck spec and generated HTML.

phases.label: Verification
phases.bottleneck_notes: Python tests reported 13 passed in 0.034s and Playwright reported 26 passed in 6.3s. Screenshot command also succeeded, but the overall verification phase wall time was not fully measured.

phases.label: Evaluation and history
phases.bottleneck_notes: Prepared grounding, omission, request trace, work summary, and evaluator inputs.

phases.label: Commit and push
phases.bottleneck_notes: Commit and push are pending final close-out checks.

bottleneck_analysis.interpretation: The likely bottleneck is not rendering or tests, but converting a long platform history and philosophy into a coherent 30-minute script and then a compact deck.
improvement_candidates: Create a reusable long-form platform-presentation template that maps philosophy principles to slide archetypes.
Add a script-length estimator so 30-minute decks can be adjusted with measured rehearsal data.
Consider a deck-spec validator that checks slide count, note density, and source coverage for long-form talks.

evidence: Python test output: 13 tests passed in 0.034s.
